data.heading: Where it started
data.description: Pipelines that failed at 3am and waited for a person, and silent failures that produced wrong reports.

blocks.title: Business problem
blocks.body: When a pipeline failed, someone had to restart it by hand, and recovery took around three hours. Maintenance cost grew linearly with data, so more data meant more staff.

blocks.title: Technical barriers
blocks.body: Operational data sat fragmented across observability, CMDB, identity, and ticket systems. 80% of engineering effort went into keeping the lights on, with 20 hours a week spent on pipeline maintenance.

blocks.title: Agivant's role
blocks.body: Data platform engineering, multi-source ingestion, self-healing pipelines, and data quality across the consolidated warehouse

data.heading: What Agivant built
data.description: Agivant consolidated observability, CMDB, identity, and ticket data into one governed Snowflake warehouse, then built the agent layer on top of it. The platform takes in data from enterprise applications, cloud storage, APIs, Kubernetes, and operational systems through efficient, low-latency pipelines, processing 250GB+ of new data every week. A self-healing framework recovers failures automatically within minutes, anomaly detection stops bad data at the source, and workflows are orchestrated and monitored automatically. Value in days and weeks.

blocks.title: Reporting and business communications

blocks.title: After

data.heading: Proof in production
data.description: A pipeline fails at 3am and the self-healing framework recovers it within minutes, so data stays available to executives. Anomaly detection stops bad data at the source, which gives the business every report on time and more confidence in the GenAI outputs built on the same data. Pipeline upkeep dropped from 20 engineering hours a week to 4, edge cases only, and 80% of engineering effort now goes into new AI and ML features.

blocks.heading: Measured results
